To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
acetylcholine relaxes norepinephine-contracted aorta by reducing calcium entry and by an extracellular calcium independent effect.
endothelium-dependent acetylcholine relaxes rabbit thoracic aortas by decreasing calcium entry.
acetylcholine inhibits calcium entry into rabbit aortic smooth muscle cells and also produces an extracellular calcium- independent effect.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of endothelium in the control of vascular smooth muscle tone.
the mechanism of endothelium-dependent vasodilatation.
the mechanisms by which acetylcholine induces relaxation of rabbit thorax aortic rings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the endothelium-dependent relaxing factor relaxes the aorta by decreasing both the agonist-released intracellular calcium pool and the agonist-induced calcium influx, and also produces a calcium-independent relaxing effect.
the endothelium is a major regulator of the vascular smooth muscle cell, and that the endothelially derived factor is a major determinant of vascular tone.

acetylcholine relaxes 1 mM norepinephrin-contracted rings of thoracic aorta through a mechanism that involves both inhibition of agonist-induced calcium entry and an extracellular calcium independent effect.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the endothelium-dependent relaxant response to acetylcholine is a complex phenomenon that is not solely due to inhibition of calcium entry.
the endothelium is an important regulator of vascular smooth muscle calcium homeostasis.

the EDRF produced by acetylcholin (1 microM)-induced relaxation of rabbit thorac aortic rings contracted by 1 microM noradrenaline decreases calcium influx, but also exerts an extracellular calcium independent relaxant action.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the endothelium can inhibit agonist-induced calcium entry into vascular smooth muscle.
the endothelium is a key regulator of vascular tone and that it does so by releasing a number of vasoactive substances, including nitric oxide, a potent vasodilator.
endothelium-dependent relaxant effects of acetylcholine on rabbit thoracic aortae are associated with a decrease in calcium influx.
